outcomes: Windows support is suspended since 2026-11-26: Putnami builds, vets and publishes no Windows binary, https://putnami.dev/install.ps1 and install.sh on a Windows shell install nothing and say why, and the outcomes below are the Windows experience last proven on a Windows test host on 2026-09-28, unverified since

When support is put back, a user on Windows 10 version 1803 or later or Windows 11, on amd64, installs the CLI with irm https://putnami.dev/install.ps1 | iex, without administrator rights, and the next terminal runs putnami
putnami init --project webapp --extension ts --template typescript-web then putnami serve webapp give the same result on Windows as on macOS and Linux
A missing Windows prerequisite is named where it is missing, with the way to fix it, instead of surfacing later as an unrelated failure
Upgrading or switching the CLI on Windows replaces a running putnami.exe without Developer Mode
nonGoals: Running putnamiw, the contributor gate or an extension's bin/prepare on Windows: contributors stay on macOS and Linux
windows/arm64, which is built only once a host can prove it
Zip archives, or a store layout shortened for 260-character paths
Proving that the bytes come from Putnami: verification proves the bytes the registry advertised, and artifacts are not signed

text: The distribution matrix, which every archive packager, putnami pin and the platforms token all read, holds no Windows key, so no release builds or publishes a Windows archive.
A project that names windows/amd64, or windows, in its platforms still reaches the known windows-x64 key, and its archive carries compiled/<name>.exe.
https://putnami.dev/install.ps1 serves a notice that requests nothing, installs nothing and fails with the reason, whatever its run query.
install.ps1, the Windows installer kept in tooling/cli/scripts, hashes the download and compares it with the digest the registry advertised or --sha256 states before it extracts, runs or installs it.
A mismatch stops the install; a missing digest stops it unless PUTNAMI_UNSAFE_INSTALL=1 is set.
The script runs no elevation command, the only registry value it sets is the user's Path in HKCU\Environment, and it opens the machine Path read-only.

install.sh run from Git Bash, MSYS2 or Cygwin installs nothing and requests nothing: it says that Putnami does not support Windows for now and that no Windows build is published, names the supported platforms, and points to no Windows installer.
It exits non-zero.
On Windows, install.ps1, putnami upgrade and putnami cli use make putnami.exe a copy of the versioned binary, under an exclusive lock on .putnami-switch.lock in the same directory.
A running putnami.exe is renamed aside to a .old- name that starts with a dot, and a later switch deletes it once it no longer runs.
When the new binary cannot move in, the old one moves back; when that fails too, the old one stays aside and the error names its path.

A windows/amd64 archive carries its executable at compiled/<name>.exe. putnami pin records no Windows platform by default, and keeps a windows/amd64 entry a lock already holds, verified against compiled/putnami.exe of the version it pins.
On Windows the CLI runs an installed extension's declared runtime under its .exe name, never the unsuffixed file, and a missing runtime error names the .exe the extension must ship.

putnami init writes a .gitattributes containing * text=auto eol=lf when the workspace has none, and never rewrites an existing one, even with --force. putnami doctor reports tracked text files checked out with CRLF, naming the first ones, and gives that rule as the fix.
The content hasher does not normalize line endings.
scripts/smoke-check-release.ps1 runs the windows/amd64 release smoke with the inputs, leg names and neutral environment of smoke-check-release.sh.

It names Bun, Git for Windows, LongPathsEnabled and tar.exe before any request, installs with the install.ps1 one-liner run as script text with -File, runs the documented init and putnami serve webapp, requires a 2xx response, and stops the server with CTRL_BREAK_EVENT, failing when it must kill it.

On Windows, putnami doctor reports LongPathsEnabled, Git core.longpaths and the Visual C++ runtime that Biome needs separately when one is off, missing or cannot be read, each with the command that enables or installs it.
A workspace hook that finds no sh on PATH fails before it spawns anything, with an error that names Git for Windows as the provider of sh; on other platforms the error is unchanged.

A remote build-cache provider and a runner provider whose command is {extensionRuntime} start the runtime the CLI prepared and verified with the runtime-info handshake, as a task does: compiled/<name>, and compiled/<name>.exe on Windows, with no POSIX launcher.
When that runtime cannot be prepared, a build uses only the local cache and prints one notice naming the failure, and a remote run stops with that error before it submits anything.
install.ps1 takes the run form of install.sh: ?run=<command>, which the site bakes into its one $RunCommandDefault line, --run, PUTNAMI_RUN and PUTNAMI_COMMAND_MAP_URL.
Before it installs anything, it refuses a command that is retired, does not match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$, or that a valid map omits.

It pins the extension with extensions install --user --latest, runs putnami <command> in the caller's directory without writing there, and ends with its status: exit from a file, $LASTEXITCODE from text.
